1: May Mitra be propitious to us, and Varuna; may Aryaman be propitious to us. May Indra and Brihaspati be propitious to us. May Vishnu, of the far strides, be propitious to us. Homage to Brahman! Homage to you, O Vayu — you indeed are the visible Brahman; I shall proclaim you as the visible Brahman. I shall speak the right, I shall speak the true. May that protect me; may that protect the speaker.
[Taittiriya I 10 — The commission of the teacher]

Speak the truth. Practise righteousness. Do not neglect the study of the Veda. Having brought the teacher the fee he loves, do not cut off the line of progeny. Do not swerve from the truth. Do not swerve from righteousness. Do not neglect what is useful. Do not neglect prosperity. Do not neglect the study and the teaching of the Veda.
2: From this Self, verily, space arose; from space, wind; from wind, fire; from fire, water; from water, earth; from earth, herbs; from herbs, food; from food, seed; from seed, man. Man, verily, consists of the essence of food. This, indeed, is his head; this is his right wing; this is his left wing; this is his trunk; this is his support, his foundation — the self of food, the sheath of the body.

Other than this self of food is the self of breath; within the self of breath is the self of mind; within the self of mind is the self of understanding; within the self of understanding is the self of bliss. And of the self of bliss nothing further is said but this: it is the innermost, and the innermost is the least spoken of, and the least spoken of is the most true.
[Taittiriya II 6 — The fear of the knower]

On knowing the joy of that which is without speech and without mind, one fears nothing. For him who knows the bliss of Brahman, from which words return along with the mind, not having reached it — for such a one, what is there to fear? The wind blows for fear of Him; the sun rises for fear of Him; the fire and the moon and death itself run their courses for fear of Him.
3: Bhrigu, the son of Varuna, approached his father and said: Venerable sir, teach me. And Varuna said: That from which these beings are born, that by which, when born, they live, that into which, on departing, they enter — that seek to know: that is Brahman. And Bhrigu practised austerity, and he found the answer in food, and was told to ask again; and he found it in breath, and was told to ask again; and he found it in mind, and was told to ask again; and he found it in bliss — and the father said: Stop. And the stopping was the finding.

He who knows the bliss of Brahman does not distress himself with the thought: why did I not do good? why did I do evil? He who knows thus overcomes both. What he has done does not burn him; what he has not done does not burn him. He looks upon both alike — for he has passed to the other shore of both, and the other shore is the joy, and the joy is the home.
